messages:
Kari: thinking out loud — should we move from our current global token-bucket enforcement to a hybrid model (local leaky-buckets at edge + central credit-reconciliation) for abuse cases? main goals: fast per-request verdicts, predictable tail latency, and ability to dampen misbehaving tenants without full eviction.
Samir: +1 to hybrid. we’ve seen the centralized checks add ~8–12ms p95 in the fast path. local buckets let the proxy accept/deny synchronously. central ledger can run async reconciliation and long-term penalties.
Lucy: tradeoffs: local buckets risk split-brain where bursts bypass central limits. central credits need bounded staleness. we should define acceptable divergence window (e.g., 30s) and actuate conservative fallbacks when the central is stale.
Anya: migration question — how do we preserve existing quota billing and metrics? we need to emit the same token_consumed events and ensure rollbacks are idempotent. also: customer-facing SLOs mustn't regress during rollout.
Kari: rough sketch config for a node (WIP):
```yaml
enforcement:
  local_bucket:
    capacity: 1000
    refill_per_sec: 50
  central_credits:
    sync_interval_s: 15
    decay_rate_per_min: 0.05
safety_mode: HYBRID
fallback_on_stale: QUEUE_ISOLATION
```
Samir: that looks good. two key implementation bits: 1) local should expose a short-lived provisional reservation token (uuid) so central can later reconcile and either charge or mark rollback, 2) reconciliation must be sharded to avoid hot central keys.
Lucy: + testing note — create a chaos test that drops central sync for 60s and verify tail latency, error rates, and cost accounting. also add a canary flag to enable only for <5% of tenants.
Anya: ops plan: canary on Dedicated -> monitor token-level deltas, billing deltas, p999 latency. if mismatch >2% we auto-disable hybrid for that shard. add dashboards: central lag, reconciliation failures, provisional-token rollbacks.
infra-bot: deploy:hybrid-enforce v0.1 rolled to infra-canary at 1923456810 :white_check_mark:
Samir: final thought — abuse mitigation: when central detects repeated rollback patterns from a tenant, escalate to timed lockout + alert to trust/ops. want algorithm proposals? maybe exponential backoff on credit refill for offenders.
Kari: yes, please sketch the backoff rule in a follow-up. for this thread let's capture interface boundaries: local fast-path verdict, provisional token surface, central async reconciler, and safety fallback modes (queue-isolation vs degrade-to-best-effort). thanks y'all — will open an RFC draft with config + metrics next week. :thumbsup:
